full_text_en:
China CITIC Bank v. Beijing Jinggong Real Estate Development General Company — dispute over a guaranty contract

Plaintiff: China CITIC Bank. Domicile: No. 22, Chaoyangmen North Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Dou Jianzhong, President of the bank.

Agent ad litem: Xu Meng, lawyer of Beijing Laosaide Law Firm.

Defendant: Beijing Jinggong Real Estate Development General Company. Domicile: Gantang Industrial Zone, Tongzhou District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Feng Changhui, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Li, lawyer of Beijing Beidou Law Firm.

The plaintiff, China CITIC Bank (hereinafter referred to as CITIC Bank), filed an action with the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court against the defendant, Beijing Jinggong Real Estate Development General Company (hereinafter referred to as Jinggong Company), over a dispute concerning a guaranty contract.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff granted a loan of USD 500,000 to Beijing Jinhui Lighting Decoration Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinhui Company), and the defendant acted as the guarantor for this loan, agreeing that if Jinhui Company defaulted, it would repay all amounts due on behalf of Jinhui Company. Upon the expiration of the loan term, Jinhui Company failed to repay the principal and interest on schedule, and the defendant also failed to perform its guaranty obligations. Now, Jinhui Company has had its enterprise legal person business license revoked, and its assets and personnel are nowhere to be found. The defendant should bear the guaranty liability in accordance with the law. Therefore, the plaintiff requests the court to order the defendant to repay the loan principal of USD 500,000 plus interest and penalty interest, and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant's Defense: 1. Although Jinhui Company's enterprise legal person business license has been revoked, it still has the capacity as a litigant; therefore, it should be added as a defendant in this case. 2. The plaintiff's provision of the loan and opening of a foreign exchange account for Jinhui Company violated foreign exchange management laws and regulations; thus, the loan agreement should be void. 3. The loan facts alleged in this case are under investigation by the Beijing Public Security Bureau; therefore, this case should be stayed. 4. The filing date of this case is July 8, 1996. According to law, the court's review period for filing a case is seven days, so the earliest date the plaintiff could have filed the lawsuit is July 1, 1996. The defendant had already sent a letter to the plaintiff on May 23, 1996, requesting the plaintiff to exercise its litigation rights. However, the plaintiff did not file the lawsuit until one month later. Pursuant to Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning Guaranty in the Trial of Economic Contract Disputes (Fa Fa [1994] No. 8, hereinafter referred to as "Relevant Provisions on Guaranty"), which provides that "if the creditor fails to exercise its right of claim within one month after receiving a written request from the guarantor, the guarantor shall no longer bear the guaranty liability," the defendant shall no longer bear the guaranty liability in accordance with the law. 5. The statutory guaranty period is six months from the date of maturity of the principal obligation. The plaintiff filed the lawsuit after the six-month guaranty period had expired, so the defendant shall no longer bear the guaranty liability in accordance with the law.

The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

On November 10, 1994, the plaintiff, CITIC Bank, Jinhui Company, and the defendant, Jinggong Company, entered into Loan Agreement No. (94) Yin Dai Zi No. 305 (hereinafter referred to as "Agreement 305"), stipulating: CITIC Bank would provide a loan of USD 500,000 to Jinhui Company for the purchase of raw materials; the loan would bear a floating interest rate, with an annual interest rate of 5% above the one-year six-month floating USD lending rate published by the Bank of China on the two banking days prior to each drawdown, to be adjusted semiannually on June 20 and December 20 of each year; Jinhui Company was required to pay interest to CITIC Bank in USD cash on June 20 and December 20 of each year, commencing from the first drawdown date; the loan term was from the date of signing to November 10, 1995; if Jinhui Company failed to repay the principal and interest within the agreed time, CITIC Bank was entitled to charge a penalty interest of 20% above the original interest rate; Jinggong Company, as the guarantor, agreed that if Jinhui Company defaulted, it would, within 15 days of receiving a written demand from CITIC Bank, repay all amounts due in cash or USD cash on behalf of Jinhui Company.

After Agreement 305 was signed, the plaintiff, CITIC Bank, performed its obligation to disburse the loan as agreed. Upon the maturity of the loan term on November 10, 1995, Jinhui Company failed to repay the principal and interest on schedule, and the defendant, Jinggong Company, also failed to perform its guaranty obligation. On May 13, 1996, CITIC Bank sent a letter to Jinggong Company, requesting it to perform the guaranty obligation. On May 23, 1996, Jinggong Company replied by letter, stating: "We have received your letter. Our liability has been discharged. Please exercise your litigation rights."

It was further found that the plaintiff, CITIC Bank, filed the lawsuit with the court on June 21, 1996.

The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held:

Agreement 305, entered into by the plaintiff, CITIC Bank, Jinhui Company, and the defendant, Jinggong Company, does not violate the laws and regulations of the state and reflects the true intentions of the parties; it should be deemed valid. Paragraph 1 of Article 133 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Interpretation on the Guaranty Law") provides: "For guaranty conduct occurring before the implementation of the Guaranty Law, the laws, regulations, and relevant judicial interpretations in effect at the time of the guaranty conduct shall apply." Paragraph 3 provides: "For disputes arising from guaranty conduct occurring after the implementation of the Guaranty Law, where the case is still at the first instance or second instance stage after the promulgation and implementation of this Interpretation, the Guaranty Law and this Interpretation shall apply." The Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China came into effect on October 1, 1995. The guaranty conduct of Jinggong Company occurred before the implementation of the Guaranty Law, and therefore, the provisions in the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning Guaranty in the Trial of Economic Contract Disputes (hereinafter referred to as the "Relevant Provisions on Guaranty"), which were effective at that time, should apply.

Article 7 of the Relevant Provisions on Guaranty provides: "If a guaranty contract does not specify the type of guaranty liability to be borne by the guarantor, or if the specification is unclear, the guarantor shall be deemed to bear compensatory liability. When the guaranteed person fails to perform the contract, the creditor shall first request the guaranteed person to discharge the debt. If the guaranteed person's property is enforced but is still insufficient to discharge the debt, the guarantor shall bear compensatory liability." Paragraph 1 of Article 17 of the Guaranty Law also provides: "If the parties stipulate in the guaranty contract that the guarantor shall bear the guaranty liability when the debtor is unable to perform the debt, this is a general guaranty." Agreement 305 does not specify the guaranty liability; therefore, the defendant, Jinggong Company, shall bear general guaranty liability.

Paragraph 2 of Article 17 of the Guaranty Law provides: "A guarantor under a general guaranty may refuse to bear the guaranty liability to the creditor before the dispute over the principal contract has been adjudicated or arbitrated and the debtor's property has been enforced in accordance with the law but is still insufficient to perform the debt." This is the right of first objection granted by law to a guarantor under a general guaranty. Paragraph 3 of Article 17 of the Guaranty Law also specifies three circumstances under which a guarantor under a general guaranty may not exercise the right of first objection, one of which is: "The debtor's domicile has changed, causing significant difficulty for the creditor to demand performance of the debt." The Relevant Provisions on Guaranty do not address the issue of the right of first objection; therefore, in resolving this issue in this case, the relevant provisions of the Guaranty Law should be applied by reference. Since the borrower, Jinhui Company, has had its enterprise legal person business license revoked and its personnel are nowhere to be found, causing significant difficulty for the plaintiff, CITIC Bank, to demand performance of the debt, the defendant, Jinggong Company, as a guarantor under a general guaranty, may not exercise the right of first objection under these circumstances. CITIC Bank is entitled to directly request Jinggong Company to bear the guaranty liability.

The provision in Article 11 of the Relevant Provisions on Guaranty, regarding the creditor's exercise of the right of claim within one month after receiving a written request from the guarantor, should be measured by the time the creditor files the lawsuit with the court. After receiving the reply letter from the defendant, Jinggong Company, on May 23, 1996, the plaintiff, CITIC Bank, filed the lawsuit on June 21 of the same year. Therefore, CITIC Bank's lawsuit was not time-barred.

The defendant, Jinggong Company, argued that the loan contract involved in this case had been placed on file for investigation by the Public Security Bureau and that the court should stay the proceedings. Jinggong Company did not provide evidence to support this argument; therefore, it is not accepted.

Upon the expiration of the performance period under Agreement 305, Jinhui Company failed to repay the loan on time, and the defendant, Jinggong Company, also failed to perform its guaranty obligation as agreed; both constitute breach of contract. The plaintiff, CITIC Bank's claim for Jinggong Company to repay the loan principal of USD 500,000 plus interest and penalty interest is supported by facts and legal basis and should be upheld.

In conclusion, the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

1. Loan Agreement No. (94) Yin Dai Zi No. 305, entered into by the plaintiff, CITIC Bank, Jinhui Company, and the defendant, Jinggong Company, on November 10, 1994, is valid.

2. Within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, the defendant, Jinggong Company, shall repay to the plaintiff, CITIC Bank, the loan principal of USD 500,000 plus interest (calculated from November 10, 1994, to November 10, 1995, at the one-year six-month floating USD lending rate published by the Bank of China plus 5%) and penalty interest (calculated from November 11, 1995, until the principal is fully paid, at the one-year six-month floating USD lending rate published by the Bank of China plus 25%).

After the first instance judgment was announced, the defendant, Jinggong Company, refused to accept it and appealed to the Beijing High People's Court. The grounds of appeal were: 1. Article 25 of the Guaranty Law provides: "If the guarantor under a general guaranty and the creditor have not agreed on the guaranty period, the guaranty period shall be six months from the date of maturity of the principal obligation." "Within the agreed guaranty period or the statutory guaranty period specified in the preceding paragraph, if the creditor does not file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration against the debtor, the guarantor is released from guaranty liability; if the creditor has filed a lawsuit or applied for arbitration, the guaranty period shall be subject to the provisions on the interruption of the statute of limitations." Jinhui Company's loan matured on November 10, 1995, but CITIC Bank did not file a lawsuit until July 1996, demanding repayment from Jinhui Company and the assumption of guaranty liability. According to the Guaranty Law, CITIC Bank's lawsuit exceeded the six-month guaranty period. 2. The first instance court found that CITIC Bank filed the lawsuit on June 21, 1996, without any evidence. CITIC Bank's lawsuit indeed exceeded the one-month period under Article 11 of the Relevant Provisions on Guaranty. Therefore, the guaranty period had expired, and the appellant should not bear the guaranty liability.

In response to Jinggong Company's appeal, the appellee, CITIC Bank, argued: 1. The loan and guaranty conduct in this case both occurred in November 1994. Pursuant to Article 133 of the Interpretation on the Guaranty Law, the Relevant Provisions on Guaranty should apply to this case. 2. Article 29 of the Relevant Provisions on Guaranty provides: "If the guaranty contract does not stipulate the period for guaranty liability, if the statute of limitations for the principal debt is interrupted, the statute of limitations for the guaranty debt shall also be interrupted." According to this provision, the appellee's claim did not exceed the six-month guaranty period, and Jinggong Company's argument is unfounded. 3. The appellee filed the lawsuit on June 21, 1996, as evidenced by the court's case registration record. Jinggong Company cannot provide contrary evidence to refute this, and this fact should be affirmed.

Upon retrial, the Beijing High People's Court found:

The original text of the guaranty clause in Agreement 305 reads: "The guarantor agrees that when the borrower defaults, within fifteen days of receiving the lender's written demand, it shall repay all amounts due, including overdue penalty interest and other expenses, in cash or USD cash. If this clause is violated, the lender shall charge the guarantor a penalty of 0.1% of the total amount due for each day of delay until the full payment is made."

On January 20, 1997, the Beijing Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a Decision on Administrative Penalty (Jing Gong Shang Chu Zi [1997] No. 439), deciding to "revoke the Enterprise Legal Person Business License of the People's Republic of China of Beijing Jinhui Lighting Decoration Engineering Co., Ltd." The registered address of Jinhui Company on its business license was No. 32, Beiwa Village Road, Balizhuang, Haidian District, Beijing. On May 13, 2002, the Beijing Enjizhuang Police Station issued a certificate stating: "There is no address No. 32, Beiwa Village Road, Balizhuang, Haidian District, Beijing within the jurisdiction of this police station." Jinhui Company was a Sino-foreign joint venture. The Chinese investor was Beijing Jinbao Fine Chemical New Technology Company, with an investment of 60% in RMB cash and equipment; the foreign investor was Weilong Industrial Co., Ltd. (Hong Kong), with an investment of 40% in equipment and USD cash. On September 18, 1998, the Chinese investor of Jinhui Company, Beijing Jinbao Fine Chemical New Technology Company, had its business license revoked. Apart from the above, the second instance confirmed the other facts found by the first instance.

The above facts are confirmed by Agreement 305, the loan receipt, the decision on administrative penalty, Jinhui Company's business license, the cancellation certificate from the Beijing Administration for Industry and Commerce, the police station certificate, correspondence between the parties, and the trial record.

The Beijing High People's Court held:

Agreement 305 is legally valid. The appellee, CITIC Bank, disbursed the loan as agreed, and Jinhui Company was obligated to repay the loan upon maturity. The appellant, Jinggong Company, was obligated to bear the guaranty liability as agreed. Agreement 305 was signed on November 10, 1994. The loan and guaranty conduct carried out pursuant to the agreement occurred before the implementation of the Guaranty Law. Therefore, the laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations in effect at the time of the conduct should apply. The first instance court's application of the Relevant Provisions on Guaranty to handle this dispute is correct.

Agreement 305 does not specify the method of guaranty and does not clearly define the start and end of the guaranty period; this constitutes an unclear stipulation of the guaranty liability period. Article 11 of the Relevant Provisions on Guaranty provides: "If the guaranty contract does not stipulate the period for guaranty liability or if the stipulation is unclear, the guarantor shall bear the guaranty liability within the period during which the guaranteed person bears liability." The period during which the guaranteed person bears liability is two years from the date the loan matures. These two years during which the guaranteed person bears liability are also the period during which the guarantor bears the guaranty liability. The guaranty period is a preclusive period, which differs from the statute of limitations and does not admit of suspension or interruption. In this case, the maturity date of the loan of the guaranteed person, Jinhui Company, was November 10, 1995. Therefore, the period during which the appellant, Jinggong Company, bore general guaranty liability was from November 11, 1995, to November 10, 1997, a period of two years. During this period, as long as the appellee, CITIC Bank, as the creditor, asserted its right against Jinggong Company, as the guarantor, Jinggong Company was required to bear the guaranty liability. The facts show that CITIC Bank asserted its right against Jinggong Company on May 13, 1996, and filed a lawsuit against Jinggong Company on June 21, 1996. Thus, CITIC Bank's assertion of its right did not exceed the two-year guaranty period. The six-month guaranty period provided in Article 25 of the Guaranty Law is not applicable to this case. Jinggong Company's appeal that CITIC Bank's assertion of its right exceeded the six-month guaranty period is inconsistent with the law and is not supported. Jinggong Company, as the guarantor, shall bear the guaranty liability in this case.

The appellant, Jinggong Company, bears general guaranty liability in this case and is entitled to the right of first objection under the law. Unless the principal contract dispute has been adjudicated or arbitrated and the debtor's property has been enforced in accordance with the law but is still insufficient to perform the debt, a guarantor under a general guaranty may refuse to bear the guaranty liability to the creditor. However, the right of first objection may not be exercised under circumstances prescribed by law. In this case, the guaranteed person, Jinhui Company, has an unknown domicile and a revoked business license; its Chinese investor's business license has also been revoked, and the circumstances of its foreign investor are unknown. This situation has caused significant difficulty for the appellee, CITIC Bank, in demanding repayment from Jinhui Company, which falls under the circumstances described in subparagraph 1 of paragraph 3 of Article 17 of the Guaranty Law. Therefore, Jinggong Company may not exercise its right of first objection. The first instance court's finding that Jinggong Company no longer enjoys the right of first objection and its judgment that Jinggong Company bears the guaranty liability to CITIC Bank are not erroneous.

In conclusion, the appellant Jinggong Company's grounds of appeal cannot be established and should be dismissed. The first instance judgment has clear findings of fact and correct application of law and should be affirmed. In accordance with subparagraph (1) of paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Beijing High People's Court rendered the following judgment on May 20, 2002:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 33,909; property preservation fee: RMB 39,304, to be borne by the appellant, Jinggong Company.

Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 33,909, to be borne by the appellant, Jinggong Company.
